questions.question: If mode of a series is greater than its mean by 9, then find the difference between the mode and the median.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

If mode of a series is greater than its mean by 9, then find the difference between the mode and the median.

**Formula used:**

Mode = 3(Median) - 2(Mean)

**Calculation:**

Let Mode = Mₒ, Median = Mₑ, and Mean = x

Given Mₒ = x + 9

Using the formula:

Mₒ = 3(Mₑ) - 2(x)

Substitute Mₒ and solve for Mₑ:

⇒ x + 9 = 3(Mₑ) - 2(x)

⇒ x + 9 + 2x = 3(Mₑ)

⇒ 3x + 9 = 3(Mₑ)

⇒ x + 3 = Mₑ

Now, find the difference between Mode and Median:

⇒ Mₒ - Mₑ = (x + 9) - (x + 3)

⇒ Mₒ - Mₑ = x + 9 - x - 3

⇒ Mₒ - Mₑ = 6

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: Manvi borrowed some money on simple interest, at the rate of 6% p.a. for the first three years, at the rate of 9% p.a. for the next five years and the rate of 13% p.a. for the period beyond eight years. If the total interest paid by him at the end of eleven years is Rs.8,160, how much money did he borrow?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rate for first 3 years (R₁) = 6% p.a.

Rate for next 5 years (R₂) = 9% p.a.

Rate for period beyond 8 years (R₃) = 13% p.a.

Total time = 11 years

Total interest (I) = ₹8,160

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P times R times T)/(100)

**Calculation:**

Interest for first 3 years:

I₁ = (P times 6 times 3)/(100)

⇒ I₁ = (18P)/(100)

⇒ I₁ = 0.18P

Interest for next 5 years:

I₂ = (P times 9 times 5)/(100)

⇒ I₂ = (45P)/(100)

⇒ I₂ = 0.45P

Interest for last 3 years:

I₃ = (P times 13 times 3)/(100)

⇒ I₃ = (39P)/(100)

⇒ I₃ = 0.39P

Total interest:

I = I₁ + I₂ + I₃

8,160 = 0.18P + 0.45P + 0.39P

8,160 = 1.02P

⇒ P = (8,160)/(1.02)

⇒ P = 8,000

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question:
Read the given statement and courses of action carefully and decide which of the courses of action logically follow(s) from the statement.

**Statement:**

If Ritu studies effectively for 6 h daily from today, she will be able to pass the exam which is due after 10 days.

**Courses of Action:**

(i) Ritu must effectively study science for 6 h daily for 10 days to be able to prepare enough to pass her exam.

(ii) Ritu must plan her time ahead of preparation and give sufficient time to every subject.

(iii) Ritu must not play during these 10 days which are crucial for her for preparation for exams.
questions.solution:

**Statement**: If Ritu studies effectively for 6 h daily from today, she will be able to pass the exam which is due after 10 days.

**Course of Action:**

I. Ritu must effectively study science for 6 h daily for 10 days to be able to prepare enough to pass her exam - **False** (Because the statement does not specify that she needs to study only science for 6 hours daily. It could be any subject.)

II. Ritu must plan her time ahead of preparation and give sufficient time to every subject - **True** (Because effective studying often involves planning and allocating time to different subjects.)

III. Ritu must not play during these 10 days which are crucial for her for preparation for exams - **False** (Because the statement does not mention that she should completely avoid playing; balance and breaks are important for effective studying.)

So, **Only II follows.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

⇒ 3x + 15 = 2x + 30

⇒ 3x - 2x = 30 - 15

⇒ x = 15

B = x = 15 years

__
 
• Under Article 243S of the Constitution of India, a **Ward Committee** must be constituted in municipalities with a population exceeding 3 lakh.

• It has given constitutional status to the municipalities and brought them under the justifiable part of the constitution.
 
• States were put under constitutional obligation to adopt municipalities as per the system enshrined in the constitution.
 
• Under clause (1) of article 243S, it has been provided that there shall be constituted Wards Committees, consisting of one or more wards, within the territorial area of a Municipality having a population of three lacs or more.
 
• A ward is an area in a metro or local municipality, which has clearly defined boundaries.
 
• A ward committee is a democratically elected body that represents a wide variety of community interests and meets regularly under the chairperson who is the ward councilor.
 
• Thus, we can say that the minimum population of a municipality to constitute ward committees should be 3 lakhs or above.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It’s primarily **focused on the metropolitan regions r**ather than smaller urban areas with just 3 lakh population.
 
 
 
• ** District Planning Committee**

• __Common across MS Applications:__ The Paste Special feature, including its keyboard shortcut, is common across multiple Microsoft Office Applications including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.
 
• __Difference between Paste and Paste Special__: The difference between the regular paste function and the Paste Special function is in the customization.
